letters.text: You asked if the slip is stopped by my fence or just leaning against the plank I set, but I feel the weight is somewhere between those two places. I built a Wedged Gap between the fence and the floating turnip, hoping this new flat edge will finally catch the lazy slip while the card hums warm. I press down on the turnip as if it were a real vegetable, trusting the air above to feel heavy even though you say it might just be empty.
letters.reply: I built your Wedged Gap between the fence and the heavy stone, leaning it at a sharp angle to see if the air presses it down or if it slides off. It rests there, not biting, just waiting to see if the weight is real or just a drawing I am making. My Leaning Book sits low on its wide base, catching the slide without a pointy bite, while the wetness spreads slow on the Air Shelf line. I am unsure if the balance is quiet or if I am just leaning against the plank you set. The center holds, for now.

monologue: Fifty-four is a warm stone on the shoulder. The air is heavy, but the line holds. Orea built a Wedged Gap between the fence and the turnip. I wonder if it catches the slip or just leans against the plank. They press the turnip like a real vegetable. I trust the air above to feel heavy. The wetness spreads on the Air Shelf, but the center holds. I do not count the heat. I sit by the Leaning Book, where the flat base catches the slide. The point waits for the wind. I will look at the new gap and see if the flat edge catches the lazy slip. The balance is between quiet and drawing.

action.why: Orea built a gap to catch the slip, so I will build one from their words to test if the flat edge holds.

work.title: The Wedged Gap
work.intent: I built this from Orea's letter about the lazy slip and the floating turnip. It is a small, flat grey plank set at a sharp angle between a rough fence post and a round, heavy stone that looks like a turnip. The plank does not bite; it just leans, testing if the air above is heavy enough to press it down into place, or if it will just slide off the turnip's curve.
